column1: SHEET 1: WORLD LEADER QUOTES ON US-ISRAEL IRAN STRIKES (since Feb 28 2026)

column4: Quote
We are witnessing a grave threat to international peace and security. Military action carries the risk of igniting a chain of events that no one can control in the most volatile region of the world.
[Condemned] the 'use of force' by the U.S. and Israel... all member states must respect their obligations under international law. Called for "immediate cessation of hostilities and de-escalation."
The outbreak of war between the United States, Israel and Iran carries grave consequences for international peace and security. The ongoing escalation is dangerous for all. It must stop.

The United Kingdom played no role in these strikes. [Iran] should refrain from further strikes, give up their weapons programmes, and cease the appalling violence and repression against the Iranian people — [this is] the route to de-escalation and back to the negotiating table.
We all remember the mistakes of Iraq, and we have learned those lessons. We were not involved in the initial strikes on Iran and we will not join offensive action now.

President Trump has expressed his disagreement with our decision not to join the initial strikes. It is my duty to judge what is in Britain's national interest, and that is the judgement I made. I stand by it.

It is very clear that the death of Iran's Supreme Leader has not moderated the regime. In fact, their actions are becoming even more reckless, destabilising and ruthless, deliberately planned to cause destruction not only to military targets but to civilian ones.

[Called] on the U.S. and Iran to resume talks, saying they favoured a negotiated settlement. [Their] countries didn't take part in the strikes on Iran but are in close contact with the U.S., Israel and partners in the region.

We reject the unilateral military action by the United States and Israel, which represents an escalation and contributes to a more uncertain and hostile international order. We demand immediate de-escalation and full respect for international law. It is time to resume dialogue and achieve a lasting political solution for the region.
We are on the same page in terms of getting this terrible regime in Tehran away. There are too many bad guys in this world, actually.
[The developments in Iran are] greatly concerning.
[The situation is] perilous. Iran's ballistic missile and nuclear programs pose a serious threat to global security. Protection of civilians and international humanitarian law is a priority.

[The attack is] unacceptable. [China condemns] the blatant killing of a sovereign leader and the incitement of regime change. [These actions] violate international law and the basic norms of international relations.

A preplanned and unprovoked act of armed aggression against a sovereign and independent U.N. member state. [The U.S. and Israel are] hiding behind worries about Iran's nuclear program and starting a humanitarian, economic and possibly radiological catastrophe.
I was saddened to learn of the passing of Iran's Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, as a result of the attacks that took place yesterday. [I extend my] sympathies to the Iranian people.
[Pakistan] strongly condemned the unwarranted attacks against Iran [and called for] urgent resumption of diplomacy.
[I am] dismayed by coordinated Israeli-U.S. attacks on Iran. The interests of the United States are not served by this. [I urge the U.S.] not to get sucked in further — this is not your war.

[Saudi Arabia] successfully intercepted Iranian attacks that targeted the Riyadh Region and the Eastern Province. [Saudi Arabia condemns] Iranian aggression and calls on the international community to take all firm measures necessary to secure the region.
[Australia] supports the United States in its effort to stop Iran from obtaining an atomic bomb. [Iran's current leadership is] a destabilising force.
Canada supports the United States acting to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and to prevent its regime from further threatening international peace and security.

[My support] is not a blank cheque. Canada is actively taking on the world as it is, not passively waiting for a world we wish to be. We do however take this position with regret because the current conflict is another example of the failure of the international order.

The United States and Israel have acted without engaging the United Nations or consulting allies, including Canada. International law binds all belligerents. [I call for] a rapid de-escalation of hostilities.
[Commending the operation and calling Khamenei] one of the most evil, violent, and cruel individuals that human history has ever seen.

[Iran views] revenge for the attacks as its legitimate right and duty. [Khamenei was killed] at the hands of the most wicked villains in the world. [The killing is] a declaration of open war on Muslims, especially Shiites, in all corners of the world.
We will not negotiate with the United States.

column1: SHEET 2: TRUMP COMMENTS ABOUT WORLD LEADERS (since Feb 28 2026)

column4: Trump Quote / Comment
This is not Winston Churchill that we're dealing with. [Said during Oval Office meeting with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz; Starmer had declined to join the US-Israeli assault]

[Starmer was] worried about the legality of the strikes. [The UK has been] much different from others. This was the most solid relationship of all [and] now we have very strong relationships with other countries in Europe.
I am not happy with the UK.

They were unfriendly. Spain has absolutely nothing that we need. They have great people, but they don't have great leadership. We're gonna cut off all trade with Spain; we don't want anything to do with Spain.
[Effusively thanked Germany for its assistance. Praised Merz and Germany while blasting other allies that have not supported the effort.]
France has been great. They've all been great. [In contrast to UK's position.] [Said during same Oval Office session where he condemned Spain and UK.]
I got him before he got me. They tried twice. Well, I got him first. [Referring to an alleged assassination plot against Trump by Iran.]

Most of the people we had in mind are dead. So, you know, we had some in mind from that group that is, is dead. And now we have another group. They may be dead also based on reports. So, I guess you have a third wave coming in. Pretty soon we're not going to know anybody.
I guess the worst case would be, we do this, and then somebody takes over who's as bad as the previous person, right?

This is the single greatest chance for the Iranian people to take back their country. [Called on IRGC to] lay down their arms and peacefully merge with the Iranian patriots and work together as a unit to bring back the country to the greatness it deserves.
